note: The Mac: the Linux first values, with timestamps that keep their fraction (C11), until part B records the Mac. First values of the input design, section 10.1 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-vanilla-playwright-human-input-design.md), until part B (board ab-t30.7) fits them; each value names its source in sources.

sources.device.rateMs: 125 Hz, the rate of the research's X input; [7]: mice report typically at 100 Hz; part B measures the operator's device
sources.device.latencyMs: C11 STAGE_LATENCY_MS (3 to 5 ms); the design's probe M1: 4 ms before the send gave a frame phase of 5.4 to 5.6 ms
sources.path.fitts: Fitts's law, a = 250 ms, b = 110 ms a bit, 300 to 1000 ms (src/record.ts fittsMs); a lognormal spread of sigma 0.2 [18]
sources.path.arc: one main sub-movement with a bell speed (minimum jerk) along an arc to one side, 2% to 10% of the distance [17]
sources.path.corrections: 0 to 2 small corrective sub-movements in the last 10% of the time (first values; [14] models sub-movements)
sources.path.overshoot: for a move of more than 500 px, 2% to 8% past the target in about 30% of moves, then the way back (first values)
sources.path.jitter: 0.3 to 1.2 px across the path at 8 to 12 Hz, a hand's tremor (first value, no source)
sources.path.approach: the speed falls in the last part for a small target (the research, P4): a later, slower end of the bell
sources.path.start: the page's last point; with none, a random point of the viewport's middle 30% to 70%
sources.path.short: a short move (C11: at most 50 px from the page's last point, a step of mouse.move with steps): samples of the client's line at the device's rate, at 0.5 to 1.5 px/ms, with 0 to 1 px of jitter across the line (C11 shortMovePx, shortSpeedPxPerMs; design 5.1, the steps row)
sources.press.pauseMs: a lognormal, median 140 ms, from 80 to 400 ms; sigma ln(400 / 80) / 4 (the harness's reference)
sources.press.holdMs: a lognormal, median 100 ms, from 60 to 180 ms; sigma ln(180 / 60) / 4; force 0.5 [1]
sources.press.doubleGapMs: 90 to 150 ms from the first release to the second press (not measured; part B)
sources.press.spread: an offset from the target's middle, a normal with a standard deviation of 1/8 of its smaller side, at most 1/4 of it
sources.press.modifierAfterMs: the release of a click's modifier key (Playwright's ensureModifiers) 60 to 200 ms after the mouse release (C11 modifierAfterMs; design 5.1, the modifiers row)
sources.wheel: a notch of 120 px (X11); gaps of 35 to 90 ms (design 8.2, first value)
sources.population: each scope's person: factors drawn once from these spreads (design 10.4; first values until part B sets the population)
sources.population.keySpeed: a factor on the time from one key press to the next, drawn once for the scope (design 10.2 and 10.4: an average typist's mean is 239 ms, a fast one's about 120 ms [19]); the spread of the pointer's speed
sources.keys.holdMs: a lognormal per key, mean 116 ms, SD 24 ms [19] (median 116 / sqrt(1 + cv^2) = 113.6, sigma sqrt(ln(1 + cv^2)) = 0.2047), from 50 to 250 ms (C11 keyHoldMs)
sources.keys.baseMs: the base part of the time from one press to the next (design 10.2), times the person's key speed and the drift: fitted with keys.pairMs on English text (test/human-keys.test.ts, its corpus) until the share of rollover (the harness's K3 measure) reached about 25% for an average typist [19]: a share of 0.246 with a mean of 222 ms and an SD of 151 ms (the literature: 239 and 112 [19]; a lognormal with that mean and SD puts 8% of the intervals below the mean hold, so it cannot give 25% of rollover); key speed 0.8: 0.33, 1.25: 0.17
sources.keys.pairMs: the letter pair's part (ms, times the key speed and the drift; never below 0, so a release that is not answered early is never passed): two hands (or the space's thumb) 0, one hand 120, one finger 200, one key twice 120; the fit of keys.baseMs; part B gives each pair's own values
sources.keys.pauseMs: more time after a space (20 to 120 ms), a mark .,;:!? (80 to 250 ms) and Enter, a line's end (200 to 600 ms) (design 10.2, first values; the research's K2: longer at word and line ends [19], [20])
sources.keys.drift: the speed in a session: a factor from 0.85 to 1.15 that drifts from word to word, a random walk of its log that keeps 0.8 of its last value with a normal step of SD 0.05 (design 10.2, first value)
sources.keys.shift: a Shift rawKeyDown 45 to 95 ms before a shifted character, its release 15 to 60 ms after the release of the last key that it holds (C11 shiftBeforeMs, shiftAfterMs); the Shift of the other hand's side in 70% of cases (design 10.2, first values)
sources.keys.chord: in a chord, each modifier 40 to 120 ms before the key, the releases 20 to 80 ms apart in reverse order (C11 chordBeforeMs, chordReleaseGapMs)
sources.keys.afterReleaseMs: a key that waits for a release (the same key again, a key after the release of Shift or of a chord's modifier) goes 5 to 30 ms after it (first value)
sources.keys.fastMs: the fast end of the person's spread, 100 to 120 ms a key, with no pair part and no pause (C11 fastKeyMs; design 7.2)
sources.keys.runSlowMs: a key run at the person's speed for 12 s, then at the fast end (C11 STAGE_RUN_SLOW_MS; the answer Q2 a); keys.typeMaxMs: the typing rule's 10 s (C11 STAGE_TYPE_MAX_MS)
